description: Periodically re-runs SELECT queries against tables and views in an Amazon Redshift cluster/workgroup, optionally resuming from a cursor column tuple.

spec.sslPolicy: Uses the pgx (Postgres wire protocol) driver default sslmode; overridable via advanced.sslmode with enum disable|allow|prefer|require|verify-ca|verify-full. The DSN is built as a postgres:// URL with sslmode appended as a query param only when set.
spec.tunnelSupport: Optional SSH bastion forwarding (networkTunnel.sshForwarding). When in use the driver rewrites the connection host to localhost:5432 and starts the tunnel with local port 5432, forwarding to the configured address.

credentialModes.name: SSH tunnel private key (additive, not a database credential)

scheme.description: Optional SSH private key + ssh://user@host endpoint used only to establish the bastion tunnel; database auth is still user/password.

continuity.notes: Pure query-polling connector. It creates no server-side objects: no replication slot, no publication, no scratch/staging table, no cursor object (the SQL cursor mentioned in code comments is client-side result streaming via the pgx driver). All resume state lives in the Flow checkpoint (bindingStateV1 -> CursorNames/CursorValues/LastPolled/DocumentCount). Stopping between polls costs nothing on the customer's side and loses nothing on ours; the only consequence of a long pause is a larger first query on resume. Caveat: rows hard-deleted from an incremental (cursor) binding are never observed, and rows updated without advancing the cursor are missed — that is a correctness property of the design, not a retention window.

discovery.method: pg_catalog queries over the Postgres wire protocol (three parallel queries: relations, columns, primary keys)
discovery.querySketch: Tables: SELECT nspname, relname, CASE relkind WHEN 'r'/'p' THEN 'BASE TABLE' WHEN 'v' THEN 'VIEW' WHEN 'f' THEN 'FOREIGN' END FROM pg_catalog.pg_class JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace ON namespace oid WHERE relkind IN ('r','p','v','f') AND <schema filter>. Columns: SELECT nspname, relname, attname, attnum, NOT(attnotnull OR domain-notnull) AS is_nullable, COALESCE(base typname, typname), typtype, atttypmod-4 AS char_max_length FROM pg_attribute JOIN pg_type JOIN pg_class JOIN pg_namespace LEFT JOIN <domain base type> WHERE attnum > 0 AND NOT attisdropped AND relkind IN ('r','p','v','f') AND <schema filter> ORDER BY nspname, relname, attnum. Primary keys: SELECT nspname, relname, attname, pos.n FROM pg_namespace, pg_class, pg_attribute, pg_constraint, generate_series(1,100,1) pos(n) WHERE conkey[pos.n] = attnum AND contype = 'p' AND relkind = 'r' AND NOT attisdropped AND <schema filter> ORDER BY relname, pos.n. <schema filter> is either `nspname = ANY($1)` from advanced.discover_schemas or a NOT IN denylist.
excludes: VIEW relations unless advanced.discover_views is set (binding generation rejects them)
FOREIGN ('f') relations — listed by the catalog query but always rejected by resource generation as an unsupported entity type
primary-key discovery only covers ordinary tables (relkind 'r') and composite keys wider than 100 columns (generate_series(1,100) cap)
discovery.allowlist: advanced.discover_schemas, when non-empty, replaces the denylist with an exact schema allowlist

streams.name: <schema>_<table> (cursor-incremental table)
streams.cursorField: <first entry of resource.cursor; the cursor is an ordered tuple of columns, not a single field>

schedule.literal: 24h (default) | Go duration string e.g. '5m'/'6h' | 'daily at HH:MMZ'
schedule.description: resource.poll overrides advanced.poll; regex-validated as ^([-+]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?(h|m|s|ms))+|daily at [0-9][0-9]?:[0-9]{2}Z)$. Duration form waits that long after the previous poll's start time; the 'daily at' form fires once per UTC day at that time.

backfill.chunking: NOT chunked at the SQL level — there is no LIMIT/OFFSET and no keyset page size. The first query streams the entire table in one statement, ordered by the cursor tuple, and boundedness comes from client-side incremental checkpointing: a Flow checkpoint is emitted after every 1000 documents but only at a boundary where the cursor tuple changes value, persisting the PREVIOUS row's cursor so a mid-query restart cannot skip rows that share a cursor value. Watchdogs abort the poll after 30m with no first row or 5m between rows.

incremental.querySketch: SELECT * FROM "schema"."table" WHERE ("c1" > $1) OR ("c1" = $1 AND "c2" > $2) OR ("c1" = $1 AND "c2" = $2 AND "c3" > $3) ORDER BY "c1", "c2", "c3";
incremental.chunking: Same as backfill: no LIMIT. The lower bound is the lexicographic-tuple-greater-than predicate built from the persisted cursor values, which are passed as positional bind parameters ($1..$N) rather than interpolated. Upper bound is open — the query runs to end of table. Resumption between polls is entirely via the Flow checkpoint (streamState.CursorValues); if the configured cursor column list changes, the connector logs a warning and resets the stream state to a fresh backfill.

snapshot.chunking: Unchunked full table scan every poll, no ORDER BY. Row IDs restart at zero each poll; checkpoints every 1000 documents. Deleted rows are never signalled because the collection key is the source PK, so stale documents persist until overwritten.

Unchunked full re-read each poll. Because the collection key is /_meta/row_id and the row id counter restarts at zero, a refresh that returns fewer rows than the previous one emits synthetic delete documents (_meta.op = 'd') for the trailing row ids, which is why this archetype is snapshot_with_tombstone rather than plain snapshot. Requires the keyless_row_id feature flag (default on); with it off the discovered collection key is empty and the user must choose one.
Same unchunked full re-read. Views never carry a primary key in the pg_constraint discovery query (it filters relkind = 'r'), so they always fall back to the row-id key.

authTierRationale: The only credential is a Redshift username/password plus host and database name — a plain connection string the customer creates with CREATE USER / GRANT, per the connector README. No OAuth app registration, no refresh token, no AWS IAM role or temporary-credential flow (the connector does not use redshift:GetClusterCredentials or the Redshift Data API; it opens a raw Postgres-wire connection with pgx). The optional SSH tunnel adds a private key but is not an alternative auth mode and does not change the tier.

unionMisfits.description: The schema's `chunking` prompt ('how one bounded chunk is bounded') presumes a SQL-level bound. This connector has none: one poll = one unbounded SELECT, and the only bounding is client-side checkpoint emission at cursor-value boundaries every N documents, plus no-data watchdog timeouts. A dedicated shape would distinguish 'query-bounded' from 'stream-and-checkpoint' resumability, since the operational risk profile (a single multi-hour statement holding a Redshift connection) is completely different.

cursorField is a single string, but the cursor here is an ORDERED TUPLE of columns compared lexicographically, and the generated WHERE clause shape depends on the tuple's arity. Collapsing it to one field loses the resume semantics entirely.

The schedule grammar is a two-alternative regex: a Go duration string (relative to the previous poll's start) OR the literal form 'daily at HH:MMZ' (absolute UTC wall-clock). Neither maps to cron, and the two have different semantics under drift and long-running queries — the duration form's next fire time is anchored to LastPolled, so a poll longer than the interval simply runs back-to-back.

Excludes is a flat string list, but the real exclusions come from three different layers: a schema denylist in SQL, a relkind filter in SQL, and an entity-type rejection in Go resource generation (FOREIGN always, VIEW conditionally). A reader cannot tell which are hard vs. configurable.

sslPolicy is a free-text string, but the meaningful facts are (a) there is no connector-side default — sslmode is only added to the DSN when the user sets it, so the pgx library default applies, and (b) the enum includes 'disable'. A structured shape would make the insecure-by-omission case explicit.

abstained.streams[].name: There is no literal stream list — every binding comes from the customer's own catalog. Names shown are the recommendation algorithm's output shape (lowercased schema_table, non-alphanumerics replaced with underscore, 'public'/'dbo' schema prefix omitted), not real streams.
abstained.streams[].cursorField: The connector ships NO cursor heuristic whatsoever: generateRedshiftResource emits discovered bindings with an empty Cursor list, so every discovered binding is full-refresh until a human edits the resource config. There is no updated_at/id sniffing to report.
abstained.streams[].supportedSyncModes: Incremental is available for any binding whose cursor list a human populates; the code does not restrict which columns are eligible, and does not verify monotonicity. Whether a given discovered table supports incremental is therefore a property of the data, not of the connector.
abstained.sharedCodeWithPostgresBatch: Not determinable from this directory alone. driver.go and discovery.go here define BatchSQLDriver, discoverTables/discoverColumns/discoverPrimaryKeys and generateCollectionSchema in `package main` with no import of any postgres-batch package — so within this checkout there is zero shared Go code with source-postgres-batch; the sibling connector is a copy-paste fork sharing only the generic go/ helpers (go/schedule, go/encrow, go/schema-gen, go/network-tunnel, source-boilerplate). Confirming that source-postgres-batch's copies are textually identical or divergent requires reading that directory, which was out of scope.
abstained.transports[0].spec.sslPolicy: The connector never sets a default sslmode; the effective TLS behavior when the user leaves advanced.sslmode unset is whatever github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib defaults to, which is not stated anywhere in this directory.
abstained.execution.continuity.resumeWindow: No resume window exists to report — nothing expires. Left null deliberately rather than guessed.

notes_redshift_vs_postgres_batch: Redshift-specific divergences observed here, all within otherwise Postgres-shaped code: (1) default port 5439 rather than 5432 (though the SSH tunnel still binds local 5432); (2) default database name 'dev' and default user 'flow_capture', matching Redshift Serverless conventions; (3) the type map adds Redshift's VARBYTE (base64 contentEncoding, with maxLength computed as ceil(n/3)*4 to account for base64 expansion) alongside Postgres BYTEA; (4) the schema denylist includes Redshift's internal 'pg_internal' and 'catalog_history' schemas on top of the usual pg_catalog/information_schema; (5) discovery reads pg_catalog directly rather than information_schema views (the file's own doc comment still says information_schema, which is stale); (6) crucially, the capture query template uses ONLY user-designated cursor columns — there is no use of ctid, xmin, or any physical row locator for chunking or change detection, which is correct because Redshift's columnar storage exposes no such stable per-row identity. That is the main design divergence a Postgres-batch reader would expect to find and does not: full-refresh bindings genuinely re-read the whole table each poll. (7) Value translation clamps out-of-range years to 0000-01-01T00:00:00Z and maps float NaN/±Inf to strings; JSON/JSONB byte slices are passed through as raw JSON.
